column1: # Declared mutations: the perturbation each pinning citation must die under.
# Four TAB-separated fields — cited test name, tracked path, `from`, `to`. `\n` and `\t` are unescaped in the
# two substrings, so a perturbation spanning lines is still one record. Blank lines and lines opening with `#`
# `from` must occur EXACTLY once in the file it names. An anchor matching twice names a set rather than a site,
# and `crates/kanhe/tests/pin_bites.rs` refuses to judge rather than substituting the first occurrence.
# A record is added only after it has been RUN and seen to kill the pin it names. A mutation that fails to
# perturb the pinned point reports a biting pin as a dead one — the safe direction, but it is noise, and the
# gate's own matrix is what proves the refusal rather than a record standing in for it.
# Added for every bound this window declared. Measured before they were written: 61 `PINNED-BY` citations
# were added since the last release and **no** record was, so a pin was proven to resolve and almost never
# to bite -- which is how two bounds shipped citing a test about a different stop, each found by review
# **What a window owes is its own bounds, not the standing set.** Paying a record for every citation the
# repository already carries is not affordable and paying one for each bound a window declares is, so the
# obligation rides the act that creates the debt: a new bound owes a record.
# No count is written here, and the reason is that one was. A figure typed into this header named how many
# bounds the window had declared: true on the day it was typed, and an understatement of the same set
# before the window closed -- in the file whose own subject is that a hand-written figure outlives its
# measurement. `pin_bites` prints the figures on every clean run (`N declared mutation(s) covering N of M
# cited test(s)`), so a reader takes them from the run rather than from a comment that can disagree with it.
